timeline.text: National park, Ramsar site and World Heritage inscription.
Joumine, Ghezala and Sejnane dams built: ~40 % of the catchment and ~70 % of the lake's water supply now dam-controlled.
Tinja sluice starts regulating exchange with the Bizerte lagoon; site put on the List of World Heritage in Danger over salinity.
Removed from the Danger List after Tunisia stopped using lake water for agriculture and committed to freshwater releases.
Catchment dam storage rises from 279 to 383 million m³ (+37 %).
Removed from Ramsar's Montreux Record: officially recovered, just before this time series begins.
Fewer than 6,000 waterbirds in the January count, against a 2008 peak near 300,000.
Park director reports migrants down from ~250,000 to ~130,000 a year; smaller dams proposed as a new water source.

rules.rule: Water in this season, JRC occurrence < 60 %, inside the low (< 5 m) flood zone
WorldCover herbaceous wetland, winter NDVI > 0.42 (vigorous spring growth), summer NDVI > 0.15
Flood zone, NDVI 0.12–0.35 in both seasons with a seasonal swing < 0.15 (perennial succulents)
Flood zone, NDVI < 0.10 in both seasons, ever flooded (JRC > 0)
WorldCover 2020 and 2021 agree (cropland, or grassland outside the flood zone), JRC ≤ 5 %
WorldCover tree/shrub in both years and summer NDVI > 0.30

data_sources.name: Sentinel-2 L2A (AWS open data COGs; ESA SAFE on Google Cloud for Jan–Feb 2018)

limitations: Weak labels. Training and test labels come from rules over WorldCover, JRC water and spectral indices, so the scores show how well each model reproduces confident weak labels on unseen locations, not true accuracy. A 600-point hand-labelled gold sample (tool included) is the next step.
Freshwater versus halophytic marsh is inferred from seasonal NDVI behaviour, not from field data. It is the least certain class pair.

No official park boundary. The WDPA polygon was not reachable from the processing environment, so statistics use a basin envelope: the JRC-flooded lake component buffered by 1 km, with the Bizerte lagoon excluded.
Few seasons. Ten points per seasonal series limit the trend tests and the driver models. The gradient-boosting leave-one-year-out R² is 0.74.
No dam-storage or annual bird-census series could be obtained, so the non-rainfall share is a residual time trend, not a measured management effect.
Mixed sensors in the 40-year series: Landsat top-of-atmosphere MNDWI to 2021, then Sentinel-2 maps. The overlap years quantify the offset.
AlphaEarth embeddings are annual (2017–2025 released at the time of writing), so this baseline cannot see the wet/dry difference.
